Jan.note: Arrivals declining from peak. Stocks moving from farmer to trader hands. Prices typically firming as physical supply tightens.

Feb.note: Low arrivals. Bulk of kharif crop already traded. Prices supported by export demand for soy meal.

Mar.note: Minimal new crop arrivals. Market driven by trader inventory and crushing plant requirements.

Apr.note: Very low arrivals. Farmers retaining remaining stock or sold out. Prices typically at seasonal high ahead of new sowing.

May.note: Kharif sowing preparations begin. Seed demand active. Market prices firm as old stock is nearly exhausted.

Jun.note: Kharif sowing season underway across MP, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan. Very minimal arrivals — farmers are in their fields, not selling. Prices firm to high due to limited supply.

Jul.note: Peak kharif sowing. Near-zero arrivals from new crop. Any market transactions are residual old stocks. Monsoon progress critically watched for yield expectations.

Aug.note: Soybean crop in vegetative/reproductive stage. No arrivals from kharif crop. Market activity minimal. Traders monitoring crop condition reports.

Sep.note: Soybean crop approaching maturity. Slight pre-harvest arrivals possible from early-maturing varieties. Market watchers begin pricing in expected crop size.

Oct.note: New kharif crop harvest commences across MP and Maharashtra. Arrivals picking up rapidly. Fresh crop prices under pressure as supply returns to market.

Nov.note: Peak harvest arrival month. Maximum daily arrivals across all major soybean mandis. Prices typically at seasonal low due to peak supply. Farmers face maximum selling pressure.

Dec.note: Arrivals beginning to decline from November peak. Prices stabilizing. Processing plants running at full capacity. Export activity picks up.

Jan.note: Cotton harvest continues in Maharashtra and Telangana. High arrivals. Prices stable to slightly declining. CCI procurement may support floor prices.

Feb.note: Final picking of the season in most regions. Arrivals declining. Quality of late-picked cotton typically lower (shorter staple).

Mar.note: Cotton season winding down. Mainly old stock trading. Mills building inventory for summer. Prices typically firming.

Apr.note: Minimal new cotton arrivals. Market driven by ginned stock. Prices supported by mill demand ahead of summer.

May.note: New kharif cotton sowing preparations in Gujarat and Maharashtra. Minimal market supply. Prices typically at seasonal high.

Jun.note: Cotton sowing actively underway in Gujarat (Saurashtra) and Vidarbha. Near-zero cotton arrivals. Any market activity is residual old stock from previous season.

Jul.note: Cotton bolls forming. No new crop arrivals. Market prices reflect old stock scarcity. Monsoon distribution critically watched.

Aug.note: Cotton boll development stage. Minimal market activity. Early estimates of new crop size begin circulating among traders.

Sep.note: First picking of the new cotton crop begins in Gujarat and parts of Punjab-Haryana. Limited early arrivals with premium quality, typically commanding higher prices.

Oct.note: Cotton harvest accelerating across all major states. Arrivals rising rapidly. New crop price discovery begins in earnest.

Nov.note: Peak cotton arrival season. Maximum supply across Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Telangana markets. Prices under pressure. CCI procurement operations influence floor prices significantly.

Dec.note: Continued high arrivals, especially from Maharashtra which harvests later than Gujarat. Good quality mid-season cotton. Export parity pricing increasingly relevant.
